differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Browser re-executes all JavaScript to rebuild the DOM.
differences.rightDesc: Server state is immediately usable, no client-side re-execution needed.

differences.title: 2. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: JavaScript needs to download, parse, and execute.
differences.rightDesc: App state is restored from the server, no heavy JS parsing.

differences.title: 3. USER EXPERIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Potential for a blank screen or stale UI until JS loads.
differences.rightDesc: Content is immediately interactive and looks like the server's response.

differences.title: 4. BANDWIDTH
differences.leftDesc: Requires sending and executing significant JavaScript on the client.
differences.rightDesc: Minimizes client-side JavaScript, leading to smaller bundles.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Client's CPU works hard to re-render and attach event listeners.
differences.rightDesc: Client CPU is minimally used, preserving battery and responsiveness.

differences.title: 6. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Frameworks often handle hydration implicitly, leading to hidden complexity.
differences.rightDesc: Designed for incremental enhancement, making complexity more manageable.

differences.title: 7. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Client needs to re-fetch or re-generate state if not serialized.
differences.rightDesc: Server state is directly resumed on the client.
